## Data for Questions 1 to 3

The following are the numbers of customers served on six consecutive days at two branches of a coffee shop.

```r
branchA <- c(52, 48, 55, 51, 49, 53)
branchB <- c(31, 70, 45, 62, 38, 62)
```

---

## Question 1

:::{.callout-warning}
## Measures of Variation

For each branch, compute the range, the variance with `var()`, and the standard deviation with `sd()`.

The two branches have the same mean. Which branch is more consistent from day to day? Explain in one sentence.
:::

---

## Question 2

:::{.callout-warning}
## Coefficient of Variation

The coefficient of variation is

$$CVar=\frac{s}{\bar{X}}\cdot 100\%$$

Compute `CVar` for both branches in R.

Branch A is measured in customers per day and its manager also reports daily revenue in NT dollars. Explain in one sentence why `CVar` is useful when two variables are measured in different units.
:::

---

## Question 3

:::{.callout-warning}
## Five-Number Summary and Outliers

For `branchB`:

1. Report the five-number summary with `fivenum()`.
2. Compute the interquartile range with `quantile()`.
3. Check whether any value falls below $Q_1-1.5\,IQR$ or above $Q_3+1.5\,IQR$.
4. Draw a boxplot with `ggplot()` and `geom_boxplot()`.
:::
